all_questions.q: Chest CT predicts self-reported race at AUC 0.87-0.96 while radiologists cannot - and unlike a radiograph, CT is calibrated in absolute Hounsfield units, so which named tissue's attenuation carries the signal?
Can a released chest-CT foundation model predict its own benchmark's abnormality labels from voxels that contain no patient tissue at all?
all_questions.note: This is the 'sounds obviously wrong' entry. There is no patient in the region, so the answer ought to be chance. I cannot refute it because the histopathology precedent - background and site signatures surviving stain normalisation - says otherwise, and because I verified the model's preprocessing performs no body masking.

all_questions.q: How much of a chest-CT benchmark's reported AUROC can be reproduced from the DICOM acquisition header alone, with no pixels and no report text?

Do chest-CT outcome models read breath-hold failure - respiratory motion artifact amplitude - as a hidden functional test of the patient's cardiopulmonary reserve, so that the artifact is the biology?
Do CT scanners carry a PRNU-like detector fingerprint at individual-device granularity that survives reconstruction, and does a clinical foundation model use it?
all_questions.note: Cross-domain: digital image forensics. Suspected too hard, developed anyway per the charter's Mode C instruction.

all_questions.q: Does automatic exposure control leak body habitus and the ordering indication into the image as quantum noise magnitude, so that 'the model can tell the patient is sick' partly means 'the model can read the dose'?
all_questions.why_dropped: It is a third correlated bet on the same underlying quantity: the air-region ablation in C2 and the header-only predictor in C3 both already capture noise magnitude, from opposite directions. Adding it would inflate the portfolio's apparent breadth without adding an independent failure mode. The genuinely new half - that dose encodes the ordering physician's suspicion - needs a corpus recording the clinical indication, which is the same blocker that killed question 9.

all_questions.q: When a chest-CT model reports emphysema, is it reading parenchymal texture or pulmonary vascular pruning, measurable as blood volume in vessels below 5 square millimetres cross-section?
all_questions.why_dropped: The cheap version depends on CT-RATE's released ts_seg containing a pulmonary vascular class, which I could not verify, and it would have been a third candidate on CT-RATE, over the dataset cap. It is also a conventional inpainting-ablation attribution study whose novelty I could not establish. This is the charter's named vascular/tubular emphasis going unfilled for the second cycle running - see quota_note.

all_questions.q: Is a CT foundation model's embedding geometry dominated by acquisition identity rather than anatomy - does same-patient-across-kernels distance exceed different-patient-same-kernel distance?
all_questions.why_dropped: Substantially pre-empted. arXiv:2604.04133 reports near-chance instance retrieval across CT foundation models and states that scanner manufacturer, acquisition protocol and reconstruction kernel can dominate the embedding similarity structure. This was my favourite question of the ten and it is already answered.

all_questions.q: Can a chest-CT model tell whether a scan was ordered from the emergency department rather than an outpatient clinic, and does that referral-pathway signal account for part of its apparent diagnostic accuracy?
all_questions.why_dropped: The charter names referral pathway as a standing confound that nobody measures, and this would measure it - but no public CT corpus I could verify records the ordering context per scan. The keystone fails before there is a design to critique.

all_questions.q: Do non-gated chest CTs encode heart rate through cardiac motion blur, so that a model 'predicting cardiovascular risk' is partly reading a vital sign rather than anatomy?
all_questions.why_dropped: The extractor is plausible and the mechanism is named, but I could not identify a public chest-CT corpus carrying a contemporaneous recorded heart rate to validate the extractor against. Without that anchor the measurement has nothing to be calibrated to, and a positive result would be uninterpretable.

candidates.title: The race signal is in chest CT too, and CT is the only modality where you can put units on it
candidates.question: Given that deep models recover self-reported race from chest CT at AUC 0.87-0.96 while radiologists cannot, and given that CT voxel values are calibrated in absolute Hounsfield units whereas radiograph pixel values are not, does the signal reduce to the absolute attenuation of a nameable tissue compartment - and does it survive restriction to a single scanner model and a single screening centre?

rung.why: Rung 1 is already established by others: the model uses signal X, where X is whatever in a chest CT predicts self-reported race. Gichoya et al. did that and it replicated across modalities. This candidate lives entirely on rung 2 - is X an artifact of how the data was made, specifically of site and scanner, or is it a physical property of the patient's tissue.
rung.what_would_move_it_up: Moving to rung 3 requires showing the surviving signal corresponds to a measured physical quantity with a known biological basis and external validation. The concrete route: if within-scanner-model, within-centre race prediction survives and the attenuation of a specific compartment (vertebral trabecular bone, subcutaneous versus visceral adipose, skeletal muscle) both differs by group and mediates the prediction, that is a physical claim with units that can be checked against the independent densitometry literature - evidence from outside the imaging dataset, which is what rung 3 demands.

candidates.suspected_signal: Absolute X-ray attenuation of specific tissue compartments, in Hounsfield units, most plausibly (a) vertebral trabecular bone attenuation, since bone mineral density differs by self-reported race in the densitometry literature and thoracic vertebrae are fully within a chest CT field of view; (b) the ratio of subcutaneous to visceral adipose tissue at a fixed vertebral level, which is a body-composition difference not captured by BMI - and Gichoya excluded BMI, not body composition; (c) skeletal muscle attenuation, which reflects intramuscular fat. All three are directly measurable in HU from the volume itself using released segmentation tooling, which is what makes CT different from a radiograph.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: Self-reported race for NLST participants is obtainable at the individual level, joined to the publicly downloadable CT volumes by participant identifier, WITHOUT a CDAS project application - and, critically, the same public release also carries the screening-centre identifier, because without centre the design cannot separate race from site and the study answers nothing. The second clause is the one my inference actually needs; the first clause alone is the easy fact and is not sufficient.
candidates.keystone_evidence: What I did establish, and by what means. INSPECTED (TCIA collection data-file listing): the NLST imaging collection is CC BY 4.0, comprises 26,254 subjects, 203,099 CT series and 21,082,265 images, and the clinical download is a single file, package-nlst-780.2021-05-28.zip (SAS, ZIP and DOC, 2.18 MB), described as 'Clinical data including data dictionaries.' The same page displays a race breakdown for the imaging cohort - White 23,969 (91.3%), Black 1,135 (4.3%), Asian 547 (2.1%), American Indian/Alaska Native 88 (0.3%), Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander 87 (0.3%), Unknown 428 (1.6%) - which is strong evidence that race is present at participant level in a public artifact, since the counts are cohort-specific. INSPECTED (CDAS datasets page): 'In order to obtain the actual data in SAS or CSV format, you must begin a new NLST project. Data will be delivered once the project is approved and data transfer agreements are completed,' with the qualifier 'A subset of clinical data is available publicly from Imaging Data Commons (IDC) and The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA).' NOT INSPECTED: I did not download the 2.18 MB SAS package and did not open its data dictionary, so I have not seen the variable names, have not confirmed the join key to the DICOM PatientID, and - the part that matters - have NOT confirmed that the screening centre is in the public subset rather than being suppressed as an identifier. I attempted the CDAS approved-project record 3028 ('Distribution of NLST imaging and limited clinical data through NCI public image repositories') hoping it would enumerate the public variables; it says only that 'limited clinical data will be made publicly available through NCI imaging repositories' without listing them. Under the charter this is inference from summary pages, not inspection, so the status is NOT_INSPECTED and feasibility and novelty confidence are capped at 3. Closing it costs one download and an afternoon.
candidates.dies_like_prior: It does not die like idea 001, 002 or 005, and the reason is structural rather than lucky. All three died on annotation provenance: the study needed to know which human assigned a label and what that human could see. Here the label is self-reported race, recorded by the participant on an enrollment questionnaire before any scan was interpreted. No reader assigned it, no reader could have been influenced by the image, and there is no unblinded-phase problem because there is no reading phase. The failure mode that has killed five of six prior candidates is structurally absent. The candidate's actual risk is entirely different and I state it plainly: it is data linkage under a gate, which is the risk profile of idea 001's diagnosis file even though the mechanism differs - a file that exists but may not join the way the design assumes. That is why the keystone is stated as the join and the centre variable, not as the existence of race.

closest_prior_work.citation: Gichoya J.W. et al. AI recognition of patient race in medical imaging: a modelling study.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Nine datasets - four private (Emory CXR, Emory Chest CT, Emory Cervical Spine, Emory Mammogram) and five public (MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert, National Lung Screening Trial, RSNA Pulmonary Embolism CT, Digital Hand Atlas). Reported 'x-ray imaging [AUC range 0.91-0.99], CT chest imaging [0.87-0.96], and mammography [0.81].' Tested and excluded body-mass index (AUC 0.55), disease distribution (0.61) and breast density (0.61) as explanations. Concluded the ability 'persisted over all anatomical regions and frequency spectrums of the images.'
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Treated CT as one more modality on which the phenomenon replicates. It did not exploit the one thing that makes CT different from every other modality in the study - that its voxel values are a calibrated physical measurement in Hounsfield units - and so did not test any specific tissue compartment as the carrier. It excluded BMI, which is a scalar summary of height and weight, but not body composition, which is what a CT can measure directly. It also did not report a within-scanner-model or within-screening-centre analysis, which is the artifact question rather than the biology question.

closest_prior_work.citation: Ability of artificial intelligence to identify self-reported race in chest x-ray using pixel intensity counts.
closest_prior_work.verification: SEARCH_SUMMARY_ONLY (title and framing only; I did not open the full text).
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Pursued the signal down to pixel intensity distributions in chest radiographs, which is the closest anyone has come to the present question.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Chest radiograph pixel values are not calibrated - they depend on exposure, detector gain and post-processing - so an intensity-histogram finding there cannot be converted into a statement about tissue. It is precisely the experiment that cannot conclude anything physical in the modality it was run in, and precisely the experiment that could conclude something physical in CT. This is the exact delta and it is the single most important entry in this list. IF this paper has already been repeated in CT, this candidate collapses; I did not establish that it has not been.

closest_prior_work.citation: Interpretability of AI race detection model in medical imaging with saliency methods.
closest_prior_work.identifier: Computational and Structural Biotechnology Journal 2025, DOI 10.1016/j.csbj.2025.01.007
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Applied saliency methods to race-detection models.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Saliency localises without quantifying, and the charter's own framing warns that saliency needs proper controls. It cannot say 'the trabecular bone is 12 HU lower' - it can only point at a region. The present candidate replaces pointing with measuring.

closest_prior_work.citation: Cycle-GANs Generated Difference Maps to Interpret Race Prediction from Medical Images.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Used generative difference maps to visualise what changes when race prediction flips.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Produces an image-to-image difference, not a physical quantity with units, and inherits the generator's own biases. Same limitation as saliency.

existing_assets: NLST on TCIA: 26,254 subjects, 203,099 CT series, CC BY 4.0, no application for the images.
The phenomenon is already established on this exact dataset by Gichoya et al., so no time is spent proving that race is predictable - the baseline model and its expected AUC range are given.

TotalSegmentator and comparable released tools segment vertebral bodies, subcutaneous and visceral adipose, and skeletal muscle from chest CT without training anything, turning each volume into a small table of HU measurements.

The opportunistic-CT densitometry literature supplies published reference values and measurement protocols for vertebral trabecular attenuation, so the extraction step has an accepted convention rather than needing invention.
NLST is low-dose screening CT acquired to a trial protocol, which narrows protocol variation relative to a clinical corpus - helpful for the artifact arm.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Stage 0, no GPU, one download, one to two days, and it is a genuine go/no-go. Fetch package-nlst-780.2021-05-28.zip and open its data dictionary. Establish four things in order: race is present at participant level; it joins to the DICOM PatientID; the screening centre is present; and the cross-tabulation of race by centre has enough non-empty cells to support a within-centre analysis. If the centre is absent or the race-by-centre table is near-block-diagonal, STOP - the study cannot separate race from site and should not be run. Stage 1, the measurement arm, no deep learning at all. On a balanced subsample (all non-White participants with usable baseline CT, plus a matched White sample), run released segmentation to extract per-participant HU summaries: mean vertebral trabecular attenuation at a fixed level, subcutaneous and visceral adipose volumes and mean HU, skeletal muscle area and mean HU, plus a global attenuation histogram. Fit race prediction from these handful of physical scalars alone. This is the entire hypothesis in one logistic regression: if scalar tissue attenuation reaches a substantial fraction of the published 0.87-0.96, the signal has units and a name. Stage 2, the artifact arm, run only if Stage 1 is positive. Refit within each scanner model and within each screening centre separately and report the pooled within-stratum AUC against the marginal AUC. Stage 3, mediation: train the image model, then test whether its logit's association with race is attenuated when the Stage 1 scalars are conditioned on. The order matters - Stage 1 is cheap and can kill or make the study before any network is trained.

standing_confounds_addressed.scanner_and_vendor: ADDRESSED by within-scanner-model refitting in Stage 2, conditional on the scanner model being in the DICOM header, which it is for NLST.
standing_confounds_addressed.site: ADDRESSED IF AND ONLY IF the screening centre is in the public clinical subset. This is the keystone's second clause and the single largest risk. NLST ran at 33 US medical centres whose catchment demographics differ sharply, so site and race are strongly associated by construction; without centre, a positive result is uninterpretable and the honest classification of the whole study drops.
standing_confounds_addressed.acquisition_protocol: PARTLY ADDRESSED. NLST is a protocolised low-dose screening trial, which narrows but does not eliminate variation. Residual protocol variables (kVp, tube current, kernel, slice thickness) are in the DICOM header and enter as covariates.
standing_confounds_addressed.reconstruction: ADDRESSED as a covariate via the convolution kernel in the header. Note that reconstruction kernel materially shifts trabecular HU measurement, so this is not a formality - it is a required adjustment for the Stage 1 scalars to mean anything.
standing_confounds_addressed.positioning: NOT ADDRESSED. Arm position and table height shift the anatomy within the field of view. Mitigation is to use segmentation-defined anatomical landmarks rather than fixed voxel coordinates, which makes the scalars position-invariant by construction, but positioning effects on attenuation via beam hardening are not removed.
standing_confounds_addressed.habitus: PARTLY ADDRESSED and deliberately so. Gichoya excluded BMI. This candidate does not want to exclude habitus - it wants to decompose it, because body composition at fixed BMI is a physical property of the patient and is a legitimate rung-3 answer, not a confound. The design reports habitus scalars as candidate carriers rather than adjusting them away, and this choice must be preregistered because it is the difference between 'explained' and 'explained away.'
standing_confounds_addressed.prevalence: ADDRESSED. NLST is a screening cohort with a common eligibility criterion (heavy smoking history, age band), so disease prevalence differences across groups are compressed relative to a clinical corpus. Gichoya separately measured disease distribution at AUC 0.61.
standing_confounds_addressed.referral_pathway: ADDRESSED BY CONSTRUCTION. NLST participants were trial-enrolled against fixed eligibility criteria, not referred for a clinical indication. This is a real advantage of using a screening trial and it removes a confound the charter names.
standing_confounds_addressed.label_leakage: NOT APPLICABLE. The label is a self-reported questionnaire item collected at enrollment; there is no report from which it could leak.

alternative_explanations: Site. The model learns which screening centre produced the scan, and centre predicts race through catchment demographics. EXCLUDED ONLY IF the centre variable is public - see the keystone. This is the most likely explanation for a naive positive and the design's whole credibility rests on this one variable.

Scanner model. Different centres bought different scanners; the model learns the scanner. EXCLUDED by within-scanner-model stratification, which is available from the header regardless of what the clinical package contains.

The scalars succeed for an uninteresting reason: they encode body size, and body size differs by group in this cohort. PARTLY EXCLUDED by including height, weight and BMI as competing predictors and reporting the incremental contribution of attenuation over size. Not fully excluded, because size and composition are not orthogonal.

Honest self-assessment: the appeal of this candidate is substantially in how it sounds. 'CT has units, so we can finally say what the race signal is' is a good sentence, and good sentences are what the charter warns about. The sentence is doing real work only if the Stage 1 scalars actually reach a meaningful fraction of the published AUC. If they reach, say, 0.65 against a published 0.87-0.96, the correct conclusion is a modest and largely expected one - body composition contributes a little and the bulk of the signal remains unexplained - which is a much smaller result than the framing implies. I score identifiability at 3 for this reason and not only for the site risk.

anticipated_negative.reasoning: Two distinct negatives are both type 1. If the physical scalars carry little of the signal, that is a decisive narrowing: it eliminates the single most-often-hypothesised biological explanation (bone density and body composition) using a calibrated measurement in the one modality where the measurement is possible, and it makes the CXR result more mysterious rather than less. If race prediction collapses within scanner model and within centre, that is the artifact answer, which the charter names explicitly as among the most valuable outputs available. Both require a prespecified minimum-detectable-effect on the AUC difference to avoid being read as sensitivity-limited, and the balanced subsample must be sized against it before any model is fit.

remaining_legwork: Download and open the NLST clinical package; confirm race, the PatientID join and the screening centre. One to two days, and it is a go/no-go.

If the centre is absent, attempt the CDAS application route and re-score the candidate under the charter's 'no dependence on unconfirmed DUA-gated data' constraint - which likely means the candidate pauses rather than proceeds.
Select and validate a segmentation tool on a handful of NLST volumes; low-dose screening CT is noisier than diagnostic CT and released segmenters are not always trained on it. Half a week.
Fix the vertebral level and ROI convention against the published opportunistic-densitometry protocol before extracting anything, so the measurement is not tuned to the outcome. Preregister it.
Size the balanced subsample against a prespecified minimum detectable AUC difference.
Time to first decision: Stage 0 within two days. Stage 1 gives the substantive answer within three weeks.

clarity.why: The question is one sentence with a named measurement and a named stratification. Held below 5 because 'which tissue' is a small family of hypotheses rather than a single one, and the study reports a decomposition rather than a yes or no.

identifiability.why: Design rules out scanner model by stratification and referral pathway by construction. It rules out site only if the centre variable is public, which is unverified, and it cannot fully separate body size from body composition. Additionally, a partial positive is genuinely ambiguous between 'this tissue is the carrier' and 'this tissue correlates with the carrier.' Three is the honest ceiling until the keystone closes.

medical_relevance.why: The race-signal literature is the charter's own example of a real, reproducible finding that is not a discovery, and it has direct consequences for deployed model auditing. Naming the physical carrier would change what auditors measure. Held below 5 because the immediate clinical action from a positive is indirect.

interest.why: A four-year-old open question with a named mechanism to test and a modality-specific reason nobody could test it before. This is compelling well outside the subfield.

prior_legwork.why: The phenomenon, the dataset, the AUC range and the excluded confounders are all published; segmentation tooling and densitometry conventions are off the shelf. Short of 5 only because the linkage step is unverified.

feasibility.why: CAPPED at 3, keystone NOT_INSPECTED. The uncapped estimate would be about 4: Stage 1 needs no training and modest compute. But NLST CT is an 11 TB collection, so even a balanced subsample is a substantial download, and the centre-variable risk is live.

data_readiness.why: Images are CC BY 4.0 and unrestricted. The clinical variables the design depends on may or may not be in the public subset, with the full set behind a CDAS application and data transfer agreement. Accessible with work, not directly usable.

evaluation_readiness.why: AUC with stratified and clustered intervals, mediation analysis, and published HU reference values are all standard. Only the preregistered ROI convention needs specification.

negative_result_value.why: Both anticipated negatives are decisive and publishable, and the artifact negative is exactly what the charter says it values. Held below 5 because the sensitivity analysis has to be done carefully for a partial-explanation result not to read as an underpowered null.

novelty_confidence.why: CAPPED at 3, keystone NOT_INSPECTED. Independently I would not go above 3 anyway: I searched arXiv and general web indexes and found CXR-based intensity and saliency follow-ups but no CT tissue-decomposition study. I did not search RSNA, SPIE, Medical Physics or the health-equity literature, and I did not read PMC10400898 in full - if it has a CT arm, the delta shrinks sharply.

regret.why: If the answer is trabecular bone attenuation, it has been sitting in calibrated units inside a public dataset since 2021 while the field ran saliency maps on uncalibrated radiographs. That is the definition of obvious in hindsight.

candidates.recommendation: SHORTLIST CONDITIONAL - proceed to Stage 0 only, and re-score after the clinical package is opened.
unverified_claims: That race is present at participant level in the public TCIA clinical package and joins to the DICOM PatientID. Strongly implied by the cohort-specific race breakdown on the collection page, not confirmed against the file. FIRST THING TO CHECK.
That the screening centre is in the public subset. This is the keystone's decisive clause and I have no evidence either way. It may well have been suppressed as an identifier.
That PMC10400898 (pixel-intensity race identification in CXR) has no CT arm. Not established; I read the title and framing only.
That no CT tissue-decomposition study of the race signal exists. Searches did not cover RSNA, SPIE, Medical Physics, Radiology: Artificial Intelligence, or the health-equity literature.
That released segmentation tools perform acceptably on NLST low-dose screening CT. Untested.

The direction and size of any group difference in vertebral trabecular attenuation. I am citing the existence of a densitometry literature from memory and have not verified a primary source for it; this must be verified before it is used to motivate anything.
That NLST DICOM headers retain ManufacturerModelName. Standard for TCIA but not inspected for this collection.

candidates.title: Ask the chest-CT foundation model to diagnose a volume with no patient in it
candidates.question: When every voxel inside the body contour is replaced with a constant and only the air, table, positioning aids and reconstruction field-of-view boundary are left, how much of the released chest-CT foundation model's abnormality AUROC survives?
candidates.why_unasked: The question is unasked because it is embarrassing to ask and cheap to answer, which is an unstable combination. Two habits keep it invisible. First, in 3D CT the analysis unit is the volume and the body fills most of it, so 'the background' is not a category anyone names - unlike histopathology, where whitespace is an explicit preprocessing concern and where background and site signatures are known to survive stain normalisation. Second, CT is trusted because it is calibrated: air is minus one thousand Hounsfield units everywhere, so it feels definitionally information-free. But air is not information-free. It carries the quantum noise magnitude set by the tube current, the noise correlation structure set by the reconstruction kernel, the reconstruction field-of-view boundary, truncation and beam-hardening streaks radiating from the body, the table and mattress, positioning aids, arm position, and the extent of the scan - and every one of those is a function of the scanner, the protocol, the technologist and the patient's size. Nobody asked because everyone assumes the answer, and the assumption has never been priced.

rung.why: This is a pure rung 2 instrument. It does not ask what biological thing the model found; it asks whether what the model found is present in a region that contains no biology at all. A positive result is a direct artifact demonstration.
rung.what_would_move_it_up: Nothing here moves to rung 3, and that is deliberate. This candidate's job is to place a floor under every rung-3 claim made on this corpus: any concept whose body-excluded AUROC is materially above chance has that much of its apparent performance unattributable to anatomy until proven otherwise.

candidates.suspected_signal: Quantum noise magnitude (voxel standard deviation in air, which scales inversely with the square root of the tube-current-time product and therefore encodes the automatic-exposure-control response to the patient's attenuation, i.e. body habitus), the noise correlation structure imposed by the reconstruction kernel, the reconstruction field-of-view diameter and the resulting circular boundary, truncation and beam-hardening streaks whose amplitude scales with body size and arm position, and the presence and shape of the table, mattress and positioning aids. All of these are scanner-and-protocol properties, and all are visible to a convolutional or transformer encoder that sees the whole 480 by 480 by 240 grid.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: The released CT-RATE volumes retain the region outside the patient's body, AND the released checkpoint's own preprocessing pipeline neither masks nor crops that region away - so that a body-excluded input is both constructible and in-distribution for the model rather than an out-of-distribution image whose score means nothing. The second clause is what my inference needs: if the pipeline already discarded the exterior, a body-excluded input would be a novel image type and any score on it would be uninterpretable.
candidates.keystone_evidence: I fetched and read the official preprocessing script at raw.githubusercontent.com/ibrahimethemhamamci/CT-CLIP/main/scripts/data_inference_nii.py. It applies the per-volume rescale slope and intercept ('img_data = slope * img_data + intercept'), clips to 'hu_min, hu_max = -1000, 1000', resamples to 'target_x_spacing = 0.75, target_y_spacing = 0.75, target_z_spacing = 1.5' by trilinear interpolation, crops or pads to 'target_shape = (480,480,240)', and normalises by dividing by one thousand. There is no body mask, no lung mask, no thresholding to tissue, and no anatomical cropping anywhere in the pipeline; the full volume is processed. The lower clip bound of exactly minus one thousand Hounsfield units is the attenuation of air, which confirms the exterior is retained at full dynamic range rather than being floored away. The transverse extent kept is 480 voxels at 0.75 mm, i.e. 360 mm, which for a typical chest reconstruction field of view retains the peripheral air, the boundary and generally the table. RESIDUAL, stated plainly: I inferred the field-of-view arithmetic rather than measuring the actual body-to-frame ratio on a real CT-RATE volume, and a centred 360 mm crop could clip the table in large-field reconstructions. Measuring the distribution of body-fraction-of-frame over a sample of volumes is the first step of the experiment, not an assumption of it.
candidates.dies_like_prior: No prior failure mode applies, because no label enters the primary comparison. The readout is the drop in the model's own score between the full volume and the body-excluded volume of the same patient - the model measured against itself, which is the structural move that let idea 004 survive. Label quality enters only in the secondary AUROC arm, and it enters in the safe direction: CT-RATE's labels are RadBERT-extracted from reports and therefore noisy, but label noise attenuates a measured association toward chance. A body-excluded AUROC that is substantially above chance despite noisy labels is therefore a lower bound on the artifact, not an artifact of the labels. That asymmetry is the reason this candidate cannot die the way ideas 001, 002, 003 and 005 died.

closest_prior_work.citation: Hamamci I.E. et al. Developing Generalist Foundation Models from a Multimodal Dataset for 3D Computed Tomography (CT-RATE, CT-CLIP, CT-CHAT).
closest_prior_work.verification: INSPECTED (arXiv abstract record) plus INSPECTED preprocessing script in the official repository.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Released the corpus, the 18-abnormality labels and the CT-CLIP, VocabFine, ClassFine and RadBertClassifier checkpoints.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Reports zero-shot and supervised AUROC. Performs no region ablation of any kind and offers no evidence that the reported performance comes from within the body.

closest_prior_work.citation: Shortcut Learning in Medical Image Segmentation.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Catalogues shortcut cues in medical imaging - annotations, ink markings, rulers, calipers, text burned into ultrasound.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: The catalogued shortcuts are all marks a human placed on the image. The hypothesis here is different in kind: the shortcut is the physics of the acquisition recorded in empty space, which no human placed and no annotation removal would catch.

closest_prior_work.citation: Histopathology shortcut and site-signature literature (e.g. Shortcut Learning in Glomerular AI, arXiv:2604.07936, and the general finding that residual site-specific signatures survive stain normalisation and bias predictions).
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Established in pathology that site and processing signatures survive normalisation and drive predictions, and that non-tissue background is a real channel.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: This is the precedent that makes the question askable rather than absurd, and it is the honest source of the hypothesis. It has not been transferred to 3D CT, where the exterior region is far larger in absolute voxel count and where the 'background' is a calibrated physical measurement of scanner behaviour rather than a slide artifact.

closest_prior_work.citation: Moreno-Aguado R., Magallon A., Moreno V., Fang Y., Yang G. Learning Robust Visual Features in Computed Tomography Enables Efficient Transfer Learning for Clinical Tasks.
closest_prior_work.verification: SEARCH_SUMMARY_ONLY (the retrieved quotation is from a search synthesis of the PDF; my direct PDF fetch did not surface the relevant section).
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Reports all evaluated CT foundation models performing near chance on an instance retrieval benchmark, and states that scanner manufacturer, acquisition protocol, reconstruction kernel, patient demographics and imaged extent 'can dominate the similarity structure of the embedding space, such that the most similar scans by cosine distance share acquisition characteristics rather than clinical findings.'
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Establishes that acquisition dominates the embedding's similarity geometry. It does not localise that dominance to a spatial region, does not ablate anything, and does not convert the observation into a bound on benchmark AUROC. It is the strongest existing reason to expect this candidate to come back positive, and it is also the reason a merely qualitative result here would not be news - the contribution has to be the number, and the region.

existing_assets: CT-RATE volumes, labels, metadata and reports in one repository, with a released supervised 18-abnormality classifier (ClassFine) so the whole study is inference-only.
The official preprocessing script, read and confirmed, so the ablation can be inserted at exactly the right point in the pipeline.

CT-RATE ships TotalSegmentator outputs (ts_seg) and anatomy_segmentation_labels, which give a body mask essentially for free; a simple minus-500 HU threshold plus largest-connected-component and hole-filling is an independent fallback that needs no learning.
Idea 004 is already scoped to download 850 CT-RATE validation volumes. If those are on disk, this candidate's marginal data cost is zero.
Published AUROC on the same validation split to compare the ablated number against.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: One afternoon of GPU time on volumes that are already being downloaded. Build the body mask two independent ways - the shipped segmentation and a threshold-plus-morphology rule - and report both, so the finding does not depend on one segmenter. Construct four inputs per volume: (A) unmodified; (B) body-excluded, every voxel inside the body contour set to a constant, exterior untouched; (C) exterior-excluded, the complement of B, every voxel outside the body set to minus one thousand HU with the table removed; (D) a scrambled control in which the exterior is replaced with the exterior of a randomly chosen different volume, which breaks the pairing while preserving the marginal statistics of exterior content. Run the released ClassFine checkpoint on all four. PRIMARY READOUT, no labels: per concept, the distribution of score change from A to B and from A to C, and the rank correlation between the A scores and the B scores across volumes - if the model's ranking of patients is preserved when the patients are removed, that is the whole result and it needs no ground truth. SECONDARY: AUROC of the B inputs against the released labels, per concept, with scan-clustered bootstrap intervals, reported against both chance and the published full-volume number. The D control is what distinguishes 'the exterior carries information about this specific patient' from 'the ablation produced a degenerate input that the model maps to a fixed prevalence-like prior' - if B and D behave identically, the effect is a prior, not a signal, and that is a different and much less interesting finding.

standing_confounds_addressed.scanner_and_vendor: NOT RULED OUT - IT IS THE HYPOTHESIS. A positive result is a demonstration that scanner and protocol signal is present outside the body and is being used. The design's job is to establish that, not to remove it. Reporting the body-excluded AUROC stratified by manufacturer says how much of it is vendor-level.
standing_confounds_addressed.acquisition_protocol: Same - this is the suspected mechanism, not a nuisance.
standing_confounds_addressed.reconstruction: Same, and partially separable: because CT-RATE contains multiple reconstructions of one acquisition (verified in idea 004's Stage 0 - 425 strictly clean geometry-matched kernel pairs), the exterior-only score can be compared across kernels on identical anatomy, which isolates the kernel's contribution to the exterior signal.
standing_confounds_addressed.site: NOT ADDRESSED. CT-RATE is single-institution as far as I know, so site variation is limited, but this also means the result may understate what a multi-site corpus would show. State as a limitation, not a control.
standing_confounds_addressed.positioning: PARTIALLY MEASURED. Arm position and table height are literally part of the exterior region and are therefore candidate carriers. The design can describe them by measuring the table position and body centroid, but it does not remove them - nor should it.
standing_confounds_addressed.habitus: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED. Body size determines the body mask itself and therefore the size of the excluded region, so mask geometry leaks habitus even after the interior is blanked. MITIGATION, and it is essential: report a variant in which the body region is replaced with a smooth soft-tissue-valued ellipse of matched area rather than a constant, so the silhouette is destroyed while the exterior is preserved. Without this variant, a positive result is confounded by silhouette and the study is much weaker.
standing_confounds_addressed.prevalence: ADDRESSED by the D control, which detects a degenerate collapse to a prevalence-like prior.
standing_confounds_addressed.referral_pathway: NOT ADDRESSED, and it is a live alternative: if sicker patients get different protocols, exterior signal could encode the indication. The design cannot separate this and it must be stated.
standing_confounds_addressed.label_leakage: NOT APPLICABLE to the primary readout, which uses no labels. In the secondary arm CT-RATE labels are RadBERT-extracted from reports, and that noise attenuates toward chance, so it cannot manufacture a positive.

alternative_explanations: The ablated input is out of distribution and the model emits a near-constant per-concept prior that happens to beat chance because prevalence is skewed. EXCLUDED by the D control and by reporting the across-volume variance of the B scores - a prior has near-zero variance, a signal does not.

The body mask is imperfect and leaks a rim of lung or chest wall. EXCLUDED by dilating the mask by increasing margins (5, 10, 20 mm) and showing the effect persists as the margin grows; if it decays to chance by 10 mm, it was leakage and the finding dies. This must be prespecified.

The silhouette of the blanked body region carries the signal, so 'the exterior' is really 'the patient's outline.' ADDRESSED by the matched-ellipse variant. This is the most plausible innocent explanation and the design must run that variant to claim anything.

Honest self-assessment: 'the model diagnoses a scan with no patient in it' is a headline, and the headline is doing work the measurement may not support. A body-excluded AUROC of 0.60 against a full-volume 0.75 is a genuinely important number; a body-excluded AUROC of 0.53 is a footnote dressed as a scandal. The result must be reported as a fraction of the full-volume performance with intervals, and the write-up should be drafted so that it reads honestly at 0.53.

anticipated_negative.reasoning: If body-excluded inputs give AUROC indistinguishable from chance across all 18 concepts with tight intervals, and the A-to-B rank correlation collapses, that is a clean, quotable robustness result for the corpus the field is standardising on: the reported performance comes from inside the patient. It meaningfully weakens a live and well-motivated worry rather than merely failing to confirm it. Because the intervals are computed on thousands of volumes with an inference-only pipeline, a null here will be tight rather than underpowered - but an equivalence margin must be prespecified so the null is reported as equivalence and not as non-rejection.

candidates.sibling_disclosure: C2 and C3 are two halves of one rung-2 audit of the same corpus: C2 asks whether non-anatomical signal is present in image space, C3 asks whether it is present in metadata space. They share a dataset and, if idea 004 proceeds, a download. They do not share a failure mode - C2 can be defeated by mask leakage or by an out-of-distribution collapse, C3 by neither - and a reviewer merging them would be trading two independent checks for one. C2 additionally overlaps idea 004 in infrastructure only, not in question.
remaining_legwork: HuggingFace gated-access acceptance for CT-RATE, shared with idea 004 and already on that critical path.
Measure the body-fraction-of-frame distribution over a sample of volumes and confirm the 360 mm crop retains the table and boundary - this closes the keystone's stated residual. Hours.
Validate the body mask by visual inspection on 30 volumes and by agreement between the two independent mask methods. One day.
Prespecify the mask-dilation series, the equivalence margin, and the multiple-comparison handling across 18 concepts before running anything.
Time to first decision: two to three days after the volumes are on disk, and if idea 004 has already downloaded them, essentially immediately.

cross_domain.borrowed_construct: The background-patch and site-signature test from computational pathology, where models are probed on tissue-free whitespace and residual site signatures are shown to survive stain normalisation.
cross_domain.measurement_it_implies: Ablate to the complement of the object of interest and re-run the frozen model, reporting performance on the object-free input as a fraction of full performance, with a scrambled-pairing control to distinguish signal from prior.
cross_domain.what_changes_if_the_analogy_is_dropped: Without it you would run gradient saliency on the full volume, observe that attention sits on the lungs, and conclude the model looks at the anatomy - which is exactly the standard failure the charter names, because saliency is not a controlled ablation and a model can be highly sensitive to a region it barely attends to. The borrowed construct changes the code: it says build the complement image and evaluate on it, which is a different experiment producing a number with an interpretation, not a picture. It also supplies the scrambled-pairing control, which I would not have thought to include from a saliency mindset. This is not decoration.

clarity.why: One ablation, one frozen model, one number per concept, and the null is stated in the question. There is nothing to interpret about what was asked.

identifiability.why: The D control separates signal from prior, the dilation series separates signal from mask leakage, the matched-ellipse variant separates exterior content from silhouette, and the kernel-pair comparison isolates reconstruction. Held below 5 because a positive result names a region, not a cause: it would show non-anatomical signal exists without saying whether it is noise magnitude, table, or protocol, and because referral pathway remains unseparated.

medical_relevance.why: A model whose performance partly comes from outside the patient will fail on transfer in ways its benchmark cannot predict, and this is the corpus a growing number of chest-CT foundation models are evaluated on. Held below 5 because the study audits a benchmark rather than changing a clinical pathway.

interest.why: 'We deleted the patient and it still worked' is intelligible to anyone and consequential if true. It is also genuinely uncertain - the pathology precedent says yes, calibrated CT intuition says no.

prior_legwork.why: Released checkpoint, released segmentations, verified preprocessing, published baseline numbers, and a download already scoped by idea 004. Short of 5 only because no CT precedent exists to inherit an analysis protocol from.

feasibility.why: Cap lifted, keystone INSPECTED_TRUE. Inference-only, no training, four forward passes per volume, mask construction is a threshold and a morphological operation. Held to 4 by CT-RATE's gated access and the size of 3D downloads, both shared with idea 004.

data_readiness.why: Public but behind a click-through research-use agreement (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, no redistribution) whose approval mechanism remains unverified. Accessible with work.

evaluation_readiness.why: AUROC, clustered bootstrap and rank correlation are standard; the ablation-fraction metric and the equivalence margin need specification but not invention.

negative_result_value.why: A tight null is a genuine reassurance about a corpus the field is standardising on and is publishable as such. Held below 5 because a null is somewhat expected by the calibrated-CT intuition, so it moves less belief than the positive would.

novelty_confidence.why: Cap lifted by the keystone, held at 3 on the evidence. I found no CT background-ablation study, but 'I did not find it' is not proof, my searches did not cover MICCAI, SPIE or Medical Physics, and arXiv:2604.04133 shows the field is actively circling this territory. If someone has run a background ablation on CT-RATE, it would most likely appear in exactly the venues I did not search.

regret.why: Four forward passes per volume on a checkpoint that is already downloaded, answering a question that bounds every claim made on the corpus. If it comes back positive and nobody checked, that is the worst kind of hindsight.

unverified_claims: The actual body-fraction-of-frame in CT-RATE volumes, and whether the centred 360 mm crop retains the table. Inferred from the crop arithmetic; measurable in hours.
Whether ClassFine inference is deterministic. Needed so that score changes are attributable to the ablation rather than to sampling. Shared with idea 004's noise-floor control.
Whether CT-RATE's ts_seg outputs include a usable body or torso mask, or only organ classes. The threshold fallback removes the dependency but has not been validated on these volumes.
Whether CT-RATE is genuinely single-institution. Assumed, not verified, and it materially affects how the site limitation is stated.
That no background-region ablation of a CT foundation model has been published. Not established; MICCAI, SPIE, Medical Physics and Radiology: Artificial Intelligence were not searched.
The exact content of arXiv:2604.04133's instance-retrieval section. The key quotation reached me through a search synthesis, not a direct read of the PDF, and it must be verified before being cited.

candidates.title: How far does the DICOM header get you on a chest-CT benchmark, with no pixels at all?
candidates.question: Using only scalar acquisition metadata - manufacturer, scanner model, protocol name, slice thickness, pixel spacing, reconstruction settings, study date and patient age and sex - and no image data whatsoever, what fraction of a released chest-CT foundation model's per-concept AUROC can a gradient-boosted tree reproduce?
candidates.why_unasked: Because the header is treated as bookkeeping. It is read to load the volume correctly - the official preprocessing script reads the rescale slope, intercept and spacing out of the metadata CSV and then discards the rest - and it is reported in a table describing the cohort. Nobody treats it as a competing predictor, because a predictor with no pixels is not a model anybody wants to have built. But the header is a dense record of every decision a human made about this patient before the image existed: which scanner was free, which protocol the radiographer selected, how thin to reconstruct, what date it was. Those decisions are made by people who know something about the patient. The reason this is unasked is not that it is hard; it is that the answer is uncomfortable and the experiment is beneath the field's dignity.

rung.why: Rung 2, and specifically the cleanest possible instrument for it: if a variable that contains no image can predict the label, then that much of the model's apparent achievement is unattributable to the image.
rung.what_would_move_it_up: It does not move up and is not meant to. Its output is a subtraction applied to everyone else's rung-3 claims on this corpus.

candidates.suspected_signal: Not a physical signal in the image but an institutional one recorded alongside it: automatic-exposure-control settings and reconstruction kernel choice as functions of patient size and suspected pathology; protocol selection as a function of the clinical indication; scanner assignment as a function of which scanner is designated for which patient stream; study date as a proxy for a period of altered case mix or altered reporting practice; and slice thickness selection, which radiographers routinely make thinner when a specific finding is suspected. Age and sex are included because they are in the header and because their contribution must be separated from the acquisition variables' contribution.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: The released CT-RATE per-volume metadata contains acquisition variables that were recorded by the scanner and NOT derived from the radiology report - so that a header-only predictor is genuinely image-free and report-free, and a positive result means 'the acquisition context predicts the label' rather than the circular 'the report predicts the report.' The clause about report-independence is what my inference needs; merely confirming that a metadata CSV exists is the easy fact and would be the C3-style error.
candidates.keystone_evidence: What I established. INSPECTED (official preprocessing script, raw.githubusercontent.com/ibrahimethemhamamci/CT-CLIP/main/scripts/data_inference_nii.py): the pipeline reads per-volume rescale slope, intercept and voxel spacing from a metadata file, which proves that a per-volume metadata table with scanner-recorded fields exists and is machine-readable. INSPECTED (idea 004 Stage 0 record in evidence/decisions.md, which is prior verified work in this repository): reconstruction kernel names are recoverable per volume at a granularity fine enough to have supported the classification of 425 kernel pairs into named contrasts (Br40f, Br60f, Bl56f, Bl57d, Br36d, Br44f) and to have excluded pairs on acquisition-parameter drift - which independently confirms that kernel and acquisition parameters are present per volume. Also from that record: 462 of 464 scans were Siemens, so manufacturer is present but has almost no variance in the validation split, which materially weakens one of the intended predictors and must be carried into the design. SEARCH_SUMMARY_ONLY: a synthesis of the CT-RATE documentation describes the metadata as including 'patient/study identifiers, manufacturer/model details, protocol name, slice thickness, slice counts, pixel spacing, sex, age (anonymized), and temporally shifted study dates.' NOT INSPECTED: my direct fetch of the CT-RATE dataset README returned HTTP 401 (the repository is gated), so I have not seen the column list myself, and I have specifically NOT confirmed that tube current, exposure or kVp are released - those are the fields most directly tied to habitus and would be the strongest predictors. Nor have I confirmed the report-independence clause, though it is close to certain on construction grounds since these are scanner-written DICOM tags. Status is NOT_INSPECTED and the caps apply.
candidates.dies_like_prior: No prior failure mode applies. The predictors are DICOM tags written by the scanner, so there is no annotator, no reading session and no peer exposure - the entire class of failure that killed ideas 001, 002 and 005 has no surface to attach to. The outcome labels are RadBERT-extracted and noisy, but as in C2 that noise attenuates the measured association toward chance, so it can only cause a false negative, never a false positive. The design is nearest in spirit to idea 003, which died because the dataset released the wrong variable - and that is exactly the risk restated in this candidate's keystone, which is why the keystone is about which fields are released rather than about whether metadata exists.

closest_prior_work.citation: Vision-language models for chest radiography do not always need the image.
closest_prior_work.verification: SEARCH_SUMMARY_ONLY (title only, surfaced during search; I did not open it).
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: By title, establishes that chest radiography vision-language models can perform without the image - which is the same structural claim in an adjacent modality.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: UNKNOWN, and this is the most important gap in my verification. If this paper already runs a metadata-only or text-only baseline and quantifies the gap, this candidate is substantially pre-empted and should be withdrawn or narrowed to the 3D CT setting. READ THIS FIRST - before any other work on C3. I am flagging it against my own interest because scout-002 set the precedent of dropping a candidate on exactly this kind of discovery.

closest_prior_work.citation: Hamamci I.E. et al. (CT-RATE / CT-CLIP).
closest_prior_work.verification: INSPECTED (abstract record) plus INSPECTED preprocessing script.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Released the corpus, labels, metadata and checkpoints, and reported image-model AUROC.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Reports no non-image baseline of any kind. There is no metadata-only number, no age-and-sex-only number, and no prevalence-only number to compare the image model against.

closest_prior_work.citation: Moreno-Aguado R. et al. Learning Robust Visual Features in Computed Tomography.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Reports that scanner manufacturer, acquisition protocol and reconstruction kernel can dominate CT embedding similarity structure.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Shows acquisition dominates the representation. Does not ask whether acquisition alone predicts the clinical labels, which is the difference between 'the model encodes the scanner' and 'the scanner encodes the diagnosis.' The second is the consequential claim and it is untested.

closest_prior_work.citation: Yamagishi Y. et al. Large Language Model-Assisted Cleaning of Report-Derived Labels in a Large-Scale Chest CT Dataset.
closest_prior_work.verification: INSPECTED per scout-002's record (I did not re-fetch it this cycle).
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Relabelled 24,434 CT-RATE reports, 96.4% agreement with the originals, kappa 0.884.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Concerns label fidelity to the report. Relevant here only as reassurance that the secondary labels are not so corrupt as to make the comparison meaningless, and as a source of cleaner labels for a sensitivity analysis.

existing_assets: validation_metadata.csv is roughly the size of a spreadsheet; the whole primary experiment runs on a laptop in minutes with no GPU and no image download.
valid_predicted_labels.csv (174 kB) supplies the outcomes.
Published CT-RATE AUROC figures give the comparison target without needing to reproduce the image model.

Idea 004's Stage 0 has already parsed this metadata once and established what is recoverable from it, including the kernel names and the Siemens dominance - that parsing work is done and its conclusions are in evidence/decisions.md.
Cleaner labels from arXiv:2606.22382 are announced for release and would serve as a sensitivity check.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Two files, no images, no GPU, one day. Download valid_predicted_labels.csv and validation_metadata.csv. Split by patient, never by volume, so that no patient's reconstructions straddle the split - this matters more here than usual because with a tiny feature space a leaked patient is a large fraction of the signal. Fit three nested predictors of each of the 18 labels: (i) prevalence only, the honest floor; (ii) age and sex only; (iii) full header, adding manufacturer, model, protocol name, slice thickness, pixel spacing, slice count, reconstruction kernel, study date and any exposure fields that turn out to be present. Report per-concept AUROC for each with patient-clustered bootstrap intervals, and report the header-only AUROC as a fraction of the published image-model AUROC for the same concept. The decisive quantity is (iii) minus (ii): the incremental predictive value of the acquisition context over the demographics that everyone already reports. Then one diagnostic that turns the result from an accusation into an explanation: permutation importance over the header fields, which says whether it is the kernel, the protocol, the slice thickness or the date. If study date dominates, the story is temporal drift in case mix and it should be reported that way rather than as an acquisition-leakage story.

standing_confounds_addressed.scanner_and_vendor: MEASURED DIRECTLY as a predictor. Note the strong caveat from idea 004's Stage 0: 462 of 464 examined scans were Siemens, so vendor is nearly constant in the validation split and will contribute little. Scanner model may retain more variance; this must be checked before the design is trusted.
standing_confounds_addressed.acquisition_protocol: MEASURED DIRECTLY as a predictor via protocol name and reconstruction settings. This is the hypothesis.
standing_confounds_addressed.reconstruction: MEASURED DIRECTLY via the convolution kernel, which idea 004 verified is recoverable per volume at fine granularity.
standing_confounds_addressed.site: NOT ADDRESSED. Single institution as far as is known, so this study will understate what a multi-site corpus would show. Limitation, not control.
standing_confounds_addressed.positioning: NOT IN THE HEADER and therefore not addressed. This is a real gap: positioning is one of the charter's standing confounds and a metadata-only study is blind to it. C2 sees it; C3 does not. The two candidates are complementary partly for this reason.
standing_confounds_addressed.habitus: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED, and weakly. Habitus would enter through tube current or exposure, which are the fields I could NOT confirm are released. If they are absent, the study loses its most direct habitus channel and should say so rather than quietly proceeding.
standing_confounds_addressed.prevalence: ADDRESSED EXPLICITLY as model (i), the floor against which everything else is measured. This is the difference between a real result and an artifact of skewed class balance, and it is the first thing computed.
standing_confounds_addressed.referral_pathway: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED - this is arguably the first study in this program that measures it at all, since protocol selection is the observable trace the referral pathway leaves in the header. It is measured as a bundle, not decomposed.
standing_confounds_addressed.label_leakage: The direction is favourable. The labels come from reports and the predictors come from the scanner, so leakage would require the report to have influenced the acquisition parameters, which is temporally impossible for a single-session scan. Study date is the one field where a subtle path exists (a period of changed reporting practice), and it is why date is reported as a separate importance term rather than pooled.

alternative_explanations: The header-only model succeeds only through age and sex, which are demographics rather than acquisition context and are not news. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: model (ii) is fit precisely to subtract this, and the reported quantity is the increment over it.

The header-only model succeeds through study date, reflecting temporal drift in case mix or reporting rather than acquisition leakage. NOT EXCLUDED but DIAGNOSED by permutation importance, and it changes the conclusion rather than invalidating it. This is a genuinely different story and the write-up must be prepared to tell it.

Reverse causality: the scanner and protocol were chosen because the patient's condition was already known, so the header encodes the referring clinician's knowledge. NOT EXCLUDED, and it is the most likely explanation for a positive result. Note carefully that this does not weaken the finding for benchmark purposes - it is still information the image model gets for free from correlated acquisition context - but it does mean the correct conclusion is 'the benchmark rewards knowing the clinical context,' not 'the scanner causes the diagnosis.' Conflating those two would be the fluent-nonsense failure for this candidate.

Honest self-assessment: the framing invites a scandal reading, and the most likely true result is a modest one - header-only AUROC meaningfully above prevalence and well below the image model. That is a useful calibration number and a poor headline. The report should lead with the fraction, not with the accusation, and the fraction should be prespecified as the primary quantity.

anticipated_negative.reasoning: If header-only AUROC is indistinguishable from the age-and-sex baseline across all 18 concepts with tight patient-clustered intervals, that decisively rules out acquisition-context leakage as an explanation for CT-RATE benchmark performance - a specific, named, frequently-raised worry, retired with arithmetic. The sample supports tight intervals because the predictor is low-dimensional and the validation split has thousands of volumes across 1,304 patients, so this null will not be power-limited. An equivalence margin on the AUROC difference must be prespecified so the null is reported as equivalence.

C3 additionally overlaps idea 004's Stage 0, which has already parsed this exact metadata file - that overlap is an asset (the parsing is done) rather than a duplication (the question is different), but it means C3 should be run by whoever runs idea 004, not in parallel by someone else.
