candidates.title: The breath-hold is a functional test, and the motion artifact is its result
candidates.question: Is respiratory motion artifact amplitude in a screening chest CT - a quantity every radiologist dismisses as a quality defect - an independent predictor of mortality, and does adjusting for it attenuate the prognostic performance of image models trained on the same scans?
candidates.why_speculative: The claim inverts the charter's rung 2. Normally the discovery is that an apparent biological signal turns out to be an artifact, and the study is over. Here the proposal is that a known artifact is a biological signal: the patient's inability to comply with a fifteen-to-twenty-second breath-hold is an unrecorded functional measurement of cardiopulmonary reserve, cognition and frailty, performed on every single patient who has ever had a chest CT, and thrown away every time. I have no direct evidence that anyone has used it this way, which is why it is Mode C.

rung.why: It starts at rung 1 - establishing that the signal is present and used - but its interesting structure is that rung 2 and rung 3 are unusually entangled. The signal is unambiguously an artifact in origin (it is motion blur, it is not anatomy) and the hypothesis is that it is nonetheless biologically meaningful. Rung 2's usual question, 'is it the scanner,' has a sharp answer here: motion is patient-generated, not scanner-generated, and that is exactly what must be demonstrated rather than assumed.
rung.what_would_move_it_up: Two things, both concrete. To secure rung 2: show the motion index is not simply reading protocol or scanner - a scanner with a faster rotation and pitch produces less motion for the same patient - which requires stratifying by scanner model and by scan duration. To reach rung 3: show the motion index correlates with an independent functional measure obtained outside the image. In NLST that means the spirometry, dyspnoea and comorbidity items in the participant questionnaire; a correlation with measured lung function would convert the index from a curiosity into a validated functional readout.

candidates.suspected_signal: Respiratory motion artifact, and specifically two named and separately measurable physical quantities. (1) Stair-step or discontinuity artifact at high-contrast diaphragmatic and fissural boundaries, arising because a helical acquisition samples different z-positions at different phases of a failed breath-hold; measurable as the z-direction second difference of the segmented diaphragm dome position, or as the magnitude of gradient discontinuity across adjacent reconstructed slices at the lung-diaphragm interface. (2) Edge blur at the same high-contrast boundaries, arising from motion within a single rotation; measurable as the width of the intensity transition across the lung-diaphragm and lung-chest-wall interfaces, normalised against the transition width at a stationary reference interface such as the vertebral cortex, which controls for the reconstruction kernel's intrinsic sharpness. That normalisation is the crux - without a stationary internal reference the index is a kernel detector, not a motion detector.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: Respiratory motion artifact is measurable from the reconstructed NLST volume alone at a magnitude that varies meaningfully between participants AND that is separable from reconstruction sharpness, so that the resulting index reflects the patient's breath-hold rather than the scanner's kernel - AND NLST vital status and cancer outcomes are linkable to the publicly downloadable imaging. The separability clause is the one my inference needs: an index that cannot be distinguished from kernel sharpness would predict outcome only through protocol, which is the artifact explanation and would make the whole study a scanner study.
candidates.keystone_evidence: Mode C, and the charter permits NOT_INSPECTED here. What I did establish as supporting context. INSPECTED (Scientific Reports 2019, s41598-019-48423-7, via search retrieval of its reported figure): the baseline incidence of motion artifacts and expiratory-phase scanning in chest CT was 35% (292 of 826) at the studied institution, which establishes that the phenomenon is common enough to have between-participant variance rather than being a rare event. SEARCH_SUMMARY_ONLY: 'even a single breath-hold for 20 seconds is not acceptable for senior patients or patients who have underlying lung diseases such as emphysema or pulmonary fibrosis,' which is the clinical basis for expecting the index to track disease severity. INSPECTED (TCIA collection data listing): NLST imaging is CC BY 4.0 with 26,254 subjects, and the clinical package is public. NOT INSPECTED: I have not measured a motion index on a single NLST volume, have not established that it separates from kernel sharpness, and have not confirmed that vital status is in the public clinical subset rather than requiring CDAS - the same open question as C1's keystone, and the two candidates should resolve it together in one download.
candidates.dies_like_prior: No prior failure mode applies. There is no human annotator anywhere in the design: the exposure is computed from voxels by a deterministic estimator, and the outcome is vital status and cancer incidence ascertained by trial follow-up rather than by anyone reading an image. The peer-exposure and reader-identity problems that killed idea 005 have nothing to attach to. The candidate does share C1's data-linkage risk, since both need the NLST public clinical package to contain what they think it contains, and that shared dependency should be treated as a single point of failure for two candidates rather than two independent risks.

closest_prior_work.citation: Deploying Clinical Process Improvement Strategies to Reduce Motion Artifacts and Expiratory Phase Scanning in Chest CT.
closest_prior_work.verification: SEARCH_SUMMARY_ONLY (the 35%, 292 of 826 figure was retrieved from a search synthesis; the paper itself was not opened).
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Quantified the incidence of motion artifacts and expiratory-phase scanning and intervened to reduce it.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Treats motion purely as a defect to be engineered away. The framing is entirely quality-improvement: nobody asks what the patients who moved have in common, or whether the artifact carries information about them. This is the exact inversion the candidate proposes.

closest_prior_work.citation: Motion correction for routine X-ray lung CT imaging; and deep-learning-based motion correction for chest CT (Japanese Journal of Radiology, DOI 10.1007/s11604-026-01986-8).
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Develops algorithms to remove respiratory and cardiac motion artifact from chest CT.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: The entire subfield is devoted to deleting the signal this candidate proposes to measure. Two consequences worth stating: first, the motion-correction literature is a rich source of validated motion metrics that can be repurposed as the estimator; second, if this hypothesis is right, deploying motion correction upstream of a prognostic model would silently remove predictive information, which is a concrete and checkable clinical implication.

closest_prior_work.citation: Head motion as a stable, heritable trait in MRI: Van Dijk et al. 2012; Couvy-Duchesne et al., Heritability of head motion during resting state functional MRI in 462 healthy twins (PMC4252775); Shared Genetic Factors Influence Head Motion During MRI and Body Mass Index (Cerebral Cortex 2017;27(12):5539, PMC6075600).
closest_prior_work.verification: SEARCH_SUMMARY_ONLY (heritability estimates h-squared 0.313 and 0.427 and intra-individual stability r 0.53-0.66 retrieved from search synthesis; papers not opened).
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Established in neuroimaging that in-scanner head motion, long treated as pure nuisance, is a stable individual trait, is significantly heritable, shares genetic factors with body mass index, and spuriously drives connectivity findings.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Confined to MRI and to head motion. Nobody has made the corresponding argument for respiratory motion in CT, where the physiological interpretation is far more direct - head motion's link to biology is indirect and contested, whereas breath-hold failure is close to a bedside test of respiratory function. This is the borrowed construct and the strongest reason to take the candidate seriously.

closest_prior_work.citation: Deep Learning-based Approach to Predict Pulmonary Function at Chest CT.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Predicts pulmonary function from chest CT with deep learning.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: This is the most dangerous entry for the candidate, because it is the paper whose model might already be reading motion without knowing it. It does not decompose its prediction and does not report any motion covariate. If a motion index alone recovered a substantial share of that paper's performance, the finding would be sharper than the mortality result - and the same experiment produces both.

existing_assets: NLST: 26,254 imaging subjects, CC BY 4.0, with trial-quality longitudinal follow-up including vital status, cause of death and lung cancer incidence - outcomes ascertained by the trial, not by chart review.
The motion-correction literature supplies validated motion metrics that can be adapted rather than invented.
Released lung and diaphragm segmentation tools locate the measurement interfaces automatically.
NLST participants completed questionnaires covering smoking, dyspnoea and comorbidity, which are candidate external validators for the index - if they are in the public subset.
The estimator is a handful of image-processing operations, so the exposure can be computed on thousands of volumes without a GPU.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Stage 0, estimator validation, and it must come first because everything downstream is worthless if the index is a kernel detector. Compute the motion index on volumes where the answer is independently known: CT-RATE's geometry-matched kernel pairs (425 of them, already identified by idea 004) are two reconstructions of ONE acquisition and therefore have IDENTICAL true motion but DIFFERENT kernels - so the index must return the same value on both. That is a direct, label-free specificity test of exactly the confound that would sink the study, and it is available for free because idea 004 has already found the pairs. If the index moves across kernel pairs, fix the reference normalisation until it does not, or abandon. Then a sensitivity check on a small set of volumes scored by eye for visible motion. Stage 1: compute the index across an NLST subsample, describe its distribution, and correlate it with the questionnaire items - age, smoking pack-years, dyspnoea, comorbidity - and with scan duration and scanner model. If it correlates with scanner model more strongly than with the participant's characteristics, the study is a scanner study and stops. Stage 2, the primary analysis: Cox regression of all-cause mortality on the motion index, adjusted for age, sex, smoking, BMI and scanner model, prespecified and preregistered. Stage 3, the model-attenuation arm and the reason this belongs in this program at all: train or obtain a prognostic image model on the same scans, then test whether its hazard-ratio contribution is attenuated by conditioning on the motion index. That is what converts 'motion predicts death' - which would be interesting but is somebody else's paper - into 'the image model was partly reading motion,' which is this program's question.

standing_confounds_addressed.scanner_and_vendor: ADDRESSED, and it is the primary threat. Rotation time, pitch and detector coverage differ across scanner models and directly set how much motion becomes artifact, so the same patient produces different indices on different machines. Handled by stratification, by scanner model as a Cox covariate, and by the Stage 0 kernel-pair specificity test.
standing_confounds_addressed.acquisition_protocol: PARTLY ADDRESSED. NLST is protocolised low-dose screening, which compresses variation, and scan duration enters as a covariate. Not fully removed.
standing_confounds_addressed.reconstruction: ADDRESSED HEAD-ON by the Stage 0 kernel-pair test, which is the strongest single element of this design and costs nothing extra.
standing_confounds_addressed.site: PARTLY ADDRESSED, contingent on the screening centre being in the public clinical subset - the same dependency as C1.
standing_confounds_addressed.positioning: NOT ADDRESSED. Arm position affects chest wall and diaphragm geometry and could affect edge-transition measurements.
standing_confounds_addressed.habitus: ADDRESSED as a Cox covariate via BMI, which NLST records. Body size affects both breath-hold ability and image noise, so this adjustment is essential rather than routine.
standing_confounds_addressed.prevalence: ADDRESSED by construction - NLST is a single screening cohort with uniform eligibility, so there is no case mix to differ.
standing_confounds_addressed.referral_pathway: ADDRESSED BY CONSTRUCTION. Trial enrollment against fixed criteria, not clinical referral.
standing_confounds_addressed.label_leakage: NOT APPLICABLE. Vital status is ascertained by trial follow-up years after the scan, and no report enters the analysis.

alternative_explanations: The index measures the reconstruction kernel rather than motion. EXCLUDED by the Stage 0 kernel-pair test, which is the reason that test is Stage 0 rather than a robustness check.

The index measures scanner model, and scanner model varies by centre, and centre predicts mortality through catchment population. PARTLY EXCLUDED by stratification; fully excluded only if the centre variable is public.

Motion predicts mortality only through age and smoking - older, sicker smokers move more and also die more, and the index adds nothing. THIS IS THE MOST LIKELY OUTCOME and it is handled by the adjusted Cox model. A null here is genuinely informative: it would say the artifact carries no information beyond what is already on the enrollment form, which is a clean and useful negative.

Reverse framing: the index is real and prognostic, but the image model was never using it, so Stage 3 shows no attenuation. That is a perfectly good result - it separates 'motion is informative' from 'the model used motion' - and the two-part design reports them independently.

Honest self-assessment: 'the breath-hold is a functional test hidden inside every chest CT' is the best sentence in this document and that is precisely why it deserves suspicion. The sentence would survive even if the effect size were negligible. The defence is that the design produces a hazard ratio with a confidence interval and a prespecified attenuation quantity, so the sentence cannot be reported without the number - but a reviewer should hold the authors to leading with the number.

anticipated_negative.reasoning: Graded honestly rather than optimistically. The Stage 0 estimator-validation negative would be decisive: if the index cannot be separated from kernel sharpness, the study is over and that is a clean methodological result worth recording. But the Stage 2 negative - motion index not associated with mortality after adjustment - is sensitivity-limited, because a null could reflect a crude estimator rather than an absent effect, and there is no way to distinguish an insensitive index from a genuine non-association without an external validation of the index. This is why Stage 1's correlation with questionnaire-based functional items matters so much: it is what would license reading a Stage 2 null as informative rather than as measurement failure. Without that external anchor the primary negative is uninterpretable, and the design should not be run in a form that omits it.

cross_domain.borrowed_construct: In-scanner subject motion as a stable individual trait rather than a nuisance parameter, from the fMRI head-motion literature, where motion was shown to be moderately stable within individuals across sessions (r 0.53-0.66), significantly heritable (h-squared 0.31-0.43), genetically correlated with body mass index, and a spurious driver of published connectivity findings.
cross_domain.measurement_it_implies: Treat the motion estimate as an exposure variable with its own distribution rather than as a quality flag: characterise its between-subject variance, test its within-subject stability across repeat scans, validate it against an external functional measure, and then test whether conditioning on it attenuates the association that the imaging model was reporting. NLST's annual repeat screening rounds make the within-subject stability test directly available - the same participant scanned in three consecutive years - which is the precise analogue of the fMRI test-retest design and would establish trait-ness rather than assume it.
cross_domain.what_would_change_if_the_analogy_were_dr: Without the analogy, motion is a quality-control flag and the code excludes the affected scans - which is what the entire existing chest-CT literature does, and it is why the question is unasked. Dropping the analogy changes three concrete things in the code. First, motion becomes a continuous exposure rather than a binary exclusion criterion, so it enters the regression instead of the filter. Second, the repeat-screening-round stability analysis exists at all; nobody computes the test-retest reliability of an artifact they intend to discard. Third, the attenuation analysis in Stage 3 is directly modelled on the fMRI finding that motion spuriously drove connectivity results - that is the specific published failure this candidate is checking for in a different modality, and without it there is no reason to look. This is the opposite of decoration: the analogy determines the estimand, the design and the analysis.

mechanism_clarity.why: Two specific physical quantities are named with their physical origin - stair-step discontinuity from z-sampling across a failed breath-hold, and intra-rotation edge blur - along with the exact interfaces to measure them at and the stationary internal reference that separates them from kernel sharpness. Held below 5 because the chain from the measured quantity to the claimed biology has an unvalidated link: motion artifact to breath-hold failure to cardiopulmonary reserve is inference, not measurement, until Stage 1's external correlation is done.

identifiability.why: The kernel-pair specificity test is a strong and cheap control, and the trial design removes referral pathway and prevalence outright. But scanner model, scan duration and positioning all plausibly generate the same index, and the confounding with age and smoking is severe by construction - the people who cannot hold their breath are old and sick for reasons already on the enrollment form. Three is the honest ceiling.

interest.why: It inverts the program's own framing: the charter is built around distinguishing real signal from artifact, and this proposes an artifact that is real signal. If it holds, every chest CT ever acquired contains an unrecorded functional test, and motion-correction algorithms are deleting prognostic information.

medical_relevance.why: A free functional stratifier on an examination millions of patients already receive, and a concrete warning about deploying motion correction upstream of prognostic models. Held below 5 because the incremental value over a simple symptom questionnaire is unproven and may well be nil.

clarity.why: The question names its exposure, its outcome and its attenuation test in one sentence. Held below 5 because 'motion artifact amplitude' is a family of estimators rather than a single defined quantity until Stage 0 fixes one.

candidates.priority_arithmetic: Mode C weighting: 0.30*4 (mechanism) + 0.25*3 (ident) + 0.20*5 (interest) + 0.15*4 (med) + 0.10*4 (clarity) = 1.20+0.75+1.00+0.60+0.40 = 3.95. NOTE: Mode C scores use a different weighting from Modes A and B and are NOT directly comparable to C1, C2 or C3.

feasibility.why: CAPPED at 3, keystone NOT_INSPECTED, and unlike C3 the cap is not obviously generous here. The estimator has to be built and validated before anything else happens, NLST CT is an 11 TB collection, and the outcome linkage is unverified. Per the charter this is not a demotion - Mode C is for exactly this.

novelty_confidence.why: CAPPED at 3. I found no work treating respiratory motion in CT as an exposure rather than a defect, but the searches were shallow and the pulmonary function prediction literature is close enough that someone may have noticed.

data_readiness.why: Images unrestricted and CC BY 4.0; outcome linkage shares C1's unverified dependency on the public clinical package.

evaluation_readiness.why: Cox regression and mediation are standard, but the motion index itself has no accepted definition or reference values in this use, so the primary exposure needs to be defined and defended from scratch.

negative_result_value.why: CAPPED at 2 would apply only to an uninterpretable negative; this is classified sensitivity-limited, so 2 is assigned on the merits rather than by the cap - the Stage 2 null cannot be read confidently without external validation of the index. The Stage 0 negative is decisive but it is a methodological result, not an answer to the question asked.

regret.why: If breath-hold failure is prognostic, it has been sitting in every chest CT since helical scanning began, and the field's response has been to build better algorithms for erasing it.

candidates.recommendation: REVISE - the scientific idea is the most interesting in the portfolio, but it must not proceed past Stage 0 until the kernel-pair specificity test passes and an external functional validator is identified. Without the validator, the primary negative is uninterpretable and the study should not start.
unverified_claims: That a motion index separable from reconstruction kernel sharpness can be built at all. Entirely unverified and it is the gate.
That NLST vital status and cancer outcomes are in the public TCIA clinical package rather than behind CDAS. Shared with C1 and resolvable in the same download.
That NLST questionnaire items suitable as external functional validators (dyspnoea, comorbidity, spirometry) are in the public subset. Probably the least likely of the three to be public.

The 35% motion and expiratory-phase incidence figure, and that it generalises from a diagnostic chest CT population to NLST's low-dose screening protocol with its shorter breath-hold. Search summary only; NLST scans are faster and the figure may not transfer.
The fMRI head-motion heritability and stability figures. Retrieved from a search synthesis; the primary papers were not opened and must be read before being cited.
That respiratory motion in CT has not already been used as a prognostic exposure. Not established.
Whether NLST DICOM headers record rotation time and pitch, which the scanner-confound adjustment needs.

candidates.title: Does a CT scanner have a fingerprint, and is the model reading it?
candidates.question: Do individual CT scanners leave a photo-response-non-uniformity-like detector fingerprint that survives filtered back-projection into the reconstructed volume, and does removing that fingerprint reduce a medical imaging model's ability to identify the acquisition source?
candidates.why_speculative: Because the second half has never been asked, even though the first half is largely settled in a literature that medical imaging does not read. Digital image forensics established that sensor manufacturing variation gives every camera a unique multiplicative noise fingerprint - photo-response non-uniformity - that identifies the individual device, not the model. A small group at LIRMM Montpellier carried this to CT and showed scanner identification from sensor noise across 15 scanner models from 4 manufacturers. That work is a decade old and sits in signal-processing venues. Nobody has connected it to the medical model-auditing problem, and the connection is the candidate: the field's standard defence against scanner confounding is to adjust for manufacturer and model as categorical covariates, which assumes the confound has model-level granularity. If the fingerprint is device-level, that defence is structurally insufficient and everyone's stratified analysis is under-adjusted.

rung.why: Pure rung 2, and specifically an attempt to build a better instrument for it. The charter says rung 2 is where most of the real work is; this asks whether the standard rung-2 control - stratify by scanner model - is even the right granularity.
rung.what_would_move_it_up: It does not move to rung 3 and should not claim to. Its value is that it would either validate or invalidate a control that dozens of studies, including C1 and C4 in this very portfolio, rely on.

candidates.suspected_signal: Fixed-pattern detector response non-uniformity. The physical quantity is the per-detector-element gain and offset deviation from nominal, arising from manufacturing variation in the scintillator and photodiode array and from drift between calibrations. In a third-generation rotating-gantry CT this is not a spatially fixed pattern in the reconstructed image the way PRNU is in a photograph - each detector element contributes to every voxel along a different set of rays as the gantry rotates - which is precisely why it manifests as ring and band artifacts concentric about the isocentre. That gives the extractor: high-pass the reconstructed volume to isolate the noise residual, resample the residual into polar coordinates about the isocentre, and average over the angular coordinate. Under rotation-averaging a per-detector-element deviation accumulates into a stable radial profile while patient anatomy, which has no reason to be rotationally symmetric about the isocentre, averages down. The resulting radial signature is the candidate fingerprint. The named quantity is the angularly-averaged radial noise-residual profile, and it is measurable on any reconstructed volume with no access to raw projection data.
candidates.keystone_prerequisite: A device-level identity signal must be both PRESENT in the released reconstructed volumes and CHECKABLE - meaning that either the released DICOM retains an attribute at finer granularity than manufacturer-plus-model (station name, device serial number, or an institution-plus-model combination that resolves to one machine), or the extracted fingerprints cluster into groups strictly finer than, and nested within, the recorded acquisition metadata. Without one of these the fingerprint has nothing to be validated against and any clustering is uninterpretable. Note carefully that mere presence is the easy fact and is not the keystone - checkability is what the inference needs, and it is what TCIA de-identification most plausibly removes.
candidates.keystone_evidence: Mode C, NOT_INSPECTED is permitted. What I established. INSPECTED (TCIA collection listing): LIDC-IDRI is CC BY 3.0, 1,010 subjects, 1,308 studies, 244,527 images, 124-133 GB, and 'Seven academic centers and eight medical imaging companies collaborated to create this data set which contains 1018 cases' - so multiple sites and therefore multiple machines contributed, which is the structural requirement. SEARCH_SUMMARY_ONLY (TCIA de-identification documentation): TCIA applies 'Attribute Confidentiality Profile - DICOM PS 3.15: Appendix E' with 'a DICOM PS 3.15 compliant script removing or modifying DICOM tags deemed to be unsafe.' I could NOT confirm from the documentation which specific tags survive for this collection. This matters because the DICOM Basic Confidentiality Profile ordinarily removes Device Serial Number (0018,1000) and Station Name (0008,1010) while retaining Manufacturer and Manufacturer's Model Name - which, if true here, means the checkability clause fails in its first form and the study must rely on the unsupervised-nesting form. I did not open a single LIDC DICOM header, which is the one check that settles it and which requires downloading one case. NOT INSPECTED also: whether the radial-profile extractor works at all on reconstructed clinical CT, which no evidence in my possession addresses.
candidates.dies_like_prior: No prior failure mode applies, and this is the cleanest case in the portfolio. There is no annotation of any kind: the input is pixels, the label is a DICOM tag written by the scanner, and the LIDC nodule XML - the artifact that killed ideas 001 and 005 - is never opened. Nothing in the design depends on what any human could see or when they saw it. The risk profile is entirely different: it is that the required tag was stripped for privacy, which is a de-identification risk rather than an annotation-provenance risk. Stating that distinction is the point of this field, and it is why LIDC is a safe dataset for this candidate despite being an unsafe one for concept work.

closest_prior_work.citation: Kharboutly A., Puech W., Subsol G., et al. CT-Scanner identification based on sensor noise analysis (EUVIP 2014); Improving sensor noise analysis for CT-Scanner identification (EUSIPCO 2015); Advanced sensor noise analysis for CT-scanner identification from its 3D images (IPTA 2015).
closest_prior_work.identifier: IEEE Xplore 7018385; IEEE Xplore 7362817; HAL lirmm-01379581, lirmm-01379558, lirmm-01379571
closest_prior_work.verification: SEARCH_SUMMARY_ONLY. I located all three records and retrieved the method summary and the experimental scale from search synthesis; my direct fetch of the EUSIPCO PDF returned an image-only document that could not be read, and I have no PDF text extraction available in this environment. The papers must be read before anything is built.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Analysed how the reconstruction process modifies the intrinsic sensor noise of the X-ray detectors, defined a feature set as a CT acquisition system footprint, trained an SVM classifier, and reported experiments on images from 15 different CT scanner models from 4 distinct manufacturers, demonstrating identification of the origin of CT images. Noise extraction used a wavelet-based Wiener filter, following the camera-PRNU tradition.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Three gaps, and the candidate is defined by them. First, the reported granularity is scanner MODEL, not individual device - the forensic claim that matters for medical auditing is device-level, and it is not established. Second, and decisively for this program, nobody asks whether a medical imaging model USES the fingerprint. The forensics work shows the information is present and extractable by a purpose-built classifier; it says nothing about whether a chest-CT model trained for a clinical task has learned it. Those are different claims and only the second bears on the charter. Third, it predates modern deep learning entirely and was never connected to the confounding literature.

closest_prior_work.citation: Fridrich J. et al., sensor fingerprint and PRNU camera identification literature (e.g. Sensor Fingerprints: Camera Identification and Beyond, DOI 10.1007/978-981-16-7621-5_4; PRNU-Bench, arXiv:2509.17581).
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Established PRNU as a device-unique multiplicative sensor fingerprint estimable from and detectable in arbitrary images, with reported false acceptance around 0.0024% and false rejection around 2.4%.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Photographic sensors map one element to one pixel. A rotating CT gantry does not, which is why the extractor here has to be redesigned around rotational averaging rather than borrowed. The analogy supplies the concept and the validation protocol, not the algorithm.

closest_prior_work.citation: Simulating scanner- and algorithm-specific 3D CT noise texture using physics-informed generative network models.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Models scanner- and algorithm-specific 3D noise texture, including local noise-power-spectrum estimation from phantom, air region or anatomical background.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Models noise texture at the scanner-and-algorithm level for the purpose of simulation and denoising. Does not ask about device-level identity and does not connect to model auditing. It is however the best available source for whether the radial-profile extractor is physically sensible, and it should be read before the extractor is designed.

closest_prior_work.citation: Moreno-Aguado R. et al. Learning Robust Visual Features in Computed Tomography.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did: Reports acquisition characteristics dominating CT foundation model embedding similarity.
closest_prior_work.what_it_did_not_do: Establishes that acquisition dominates at some granularity, without asking what granularity. If the answer is device-level, adjusting for manufacturer and model does not fix it - which is the practical consequence this candidate would supply.

existing_assets: LIDC-IDRI: CC BY 3.0, fully public, no application, 1,010 subjects from seven academic centres with heterogeneous scanners and protocols - genuine device diversity in a small, downloadable corpus.
Three prior papers establishing that CT scanner identification from sensor noise works at model level, with a described feature-extraction approach to build on.

The PRNU literature supplies a mature validation protocol - correlation against a reference pattern with reported false acceptance and rejection rates - which transfers directly even though the extractor does not.
Labels are free and require no annotation: they are DICOM tags.

CT-RATE's kernel pairs, already identified by idea 004, are a ready-made specificity control: two reconstructions of one acquisition share a device, so their fingerprints must match despite differing kernels.
candidates.smallest_decisive_experiment: Stage 0, and it is one case download and a header dump: read the DICOM headers of a handful of LIDC studies and determine which of Station Name, Device Serial Number, Institution Name, Manufacturer and Manufacturer's Model Name survived de-identification. This settles the keystone's checkability clause in an hour and determines which of two studies is possible. Stage 1, supervised route, available only if a device-level or institution-level tag survived: extract the angularly-averaged radial noise-residual profile from each volume, hold out scans, and test whether a nearest-reference-correlation classifier assigns them to the correct device with the PRNU literature's own metrics - false acceptance and false rejection rates against a reference pattern. Critically, the reference pattern must be built from volumes of DIFFERENT patients than the test volume, so that patient anatomy cannot contribute; this is the direct analogue of the forensic protocol and it is what makes the result about the device. Stage 1-alternative, unsupervised route, if no device tag survived: cluster the extracted fingerprints and test whether the clustering is strictly finer than, and nested within, the recorded (manufacturer, model, kVp, kernel, slice thickness) strata. Nesting is the evidence: a partition that refines the metadata partition rather than cutting across it is what a device fingerprint would produce, whereas a partition that cuts across it is a protocol effect. Stage 2, and the only stage that makes this a medical-AI result rather than a forensics replication: take a model trained on a clinical task, subtract the estimated fingerprint from the input, and measure the change in the model's ability to predict the acquisition source. If subtracting a physically-derived, patient-independent radial profile measurably reduces source predictability while leaving clinical predictions intact, then the fingerprint is a channel the model was using and a removable one - which is a mitigation, not just a diagnosis.

standing_confounds_addressed.scanner_and_vendor: THIS IS THE SUBJECT, not a confound. The contribution is to ask whether the standard vendor-and-model adjustment is at the right granularity.
standing_confounds_addressed.acquisition_protocol: THE PRINCIPAL CONFOUND, and the hardest one. kVp, tube current, kernel and slice thickness all shape the noise residual, and a machine that is always run at one protocol is indistinguishable from that protocol. ADDRESSED in the supervised route by requiring correct identification ACROSS protocol settings for the same device, which is the specific test that separates device from protocol; ADDRESSED in the unsupervised route by the nesting requirement. If a device is only ever operated at one protocol in this corpus, it is genuinely unidentifiable and must be excluded rather than counted - and that exclusion may remove most of the corpus.
standing_confounds_addressed.reconstruction: ADDRESSED by the CT-RATE kernel-pair control, where the device is held constant and only the kernel varies. A fingerprint that changes across a kernel pair is a kernel detector.
standing_confounds_addressed.site: PARTLY ADDRESSED and partly aliased. Site and device are nearly collinear - a machine lives at one site - so device-level identification cannot be distinguished from site-level identification unless a site operated several scanners of the same model, which LIDC's seven centres may or may not provide.
standing_confounds_addressed.positioning: ADDRESSED BY THE EXTRACTOR'S CONSTRUCTION. The fingerprint is defined about the scanner isocentre, not about the patient, and angular averaging suppresses anatomy. Patient position within the bore is a residual concern because it shifts anatomy relative to the isocentre, which is exactly what the different-patient reference protocol tests for.
standing_confounds_addressed.habitus: ADDRESSED by the same mechanism - the reference pattern is built from different patients, so any habitus contribution should not transfer.
standing_confounds_addressed.prevalence: NOT APPLICABLE. No clinical outcome is predicted in Stages 0 and 1.
standing_confounds_addressed.label_leakage: NOT APPLICABLE. The label is a scanner-written DICOM tag.

alternative_explanations: The fingerprint is really the protocol. THE MOST LIKELY EXPLANATION for any positive, and the design's central burden. Handled by cross-protocol identification in the supervised route and by the nesting test in the unsupervised route. If neither can be run on the available corpus, the candidate cannot conclude and should be abandoned rather than reported with caveats.
The fingerprint is really the site, aliased with the device. NOT SEPARABLE unless one site ran multiple same-model machines. Must be reported as device-or-site rather than as device.

The radial profile is dominated by beam-hardening and cupping, which depend on the patient's cross-section rather than on the detector. PARTLY EXCLUDED by high-pass filtering before polar resampling, since cupping is a low-spatial-frequency effect, and by the different-patient reference protocol. This is a real physical objection and the filter design has to answer it explicitly.

Honest self-assessment, and it is the sharpest in this portfolio: this candidate is the most at risk of being a beautiful analogy that produces a replication rather than a discovery. Stages 0 and 1 largely redo, on a public dataset, what Kharboutly et al. did in 2014-2015 - and the charter would rightly call that decoration. The ONLY part that is new to this program is Stage 2, whether a clinical model uses the fingerprint, and Stage 2 is the part I have specified least concretely and am least confident is executable. If Stage 2 cannot be made rigorous, this candidate should be scored as a methods replication and demoted accordingly. I am scoring mechanism clarity at 5 because the physical quantity and its extractor are genuinely specific, but a reviewer should press hardest exactly here.

anticipated_negative.reasoning: A negative at Stage 1 - fingerprints do not identify devices across protocol settings, or the unsupervised clustering cuts across the metadata rather than nesting within it - decisively refutes the device-level hypothesis and, usefully, VALIDATES the field's existing practice of adjusting for manufacturer and model. That is a reassuring result about a control that C1 and C4 in this same portfolio depend on, so it has immediate internal value regardless of publication. It is decisive rather than sensitivity-limited because the PRNU literature supplies established false-acceptance and false-rejection operating points to power against, so the negative can be stated as an equivalence rather than as a failure to reject. The caveat is that this holds only if the corpus contains devices operated at multiple protocols; if it does not, the result is uninterpretable rather than negative, and Stage 0 must check for this before Stage 1 runs.

cross_domain.borrowed_construct: Photo-response non-uniformity from digital image forensics: a device-unique multiplicative sensor fingerprint, estimable from arbitrary images, used to attribute an image to an individual camera with quantified false acceptance and false rejection rates.
cross_domain.measurement_it_implies: Estimate a per-device reference pattern by aggregating noise residuals across multiple images from that device; attribute a held-out image by correlation against each reference; report the full detection operating characteristic rather than an accuracy figure; and - the part specific to CT - redesign the residual extraction around rotational averaging about the isocentre, because the detector-to-voxel mapping rotates whereas a camera's is fixed.
cross_domain.what_would_change_if_the_analogy_were_dr: Without it you would add scanner manufacturer and model as categorical covariates and consider the confound handled, which is what the medical imaging literature does now. Dropping the analogy changes four concrete things. First, the granularity of the claim: PRNU asserts device-level identity, which predicts that model-level adjustment is insufficient - a falsifiable prediction that a categorical-covariate framing cannot even state. Second, the extractor: rotational averaging of a high-passed residual about the isocentre is a specific operation on the volume that nobody would write without the fingerprint hypothesis. Third, the validation protocol: building the reference from DIFFERENT patients than the test image, and reporting false acceptance and rejection rather than classification accuracy, comes straight from forensics and is the thing that makes the result about the device rather than about anatomy. Fourth, and most importantly, the mitigation: PRNU is SUBTRACTABLE, so the analogy implies a removal experiment (Stage 2) rather than only a detection experiment. A covariate-adjustment framing implies no image-domain intervention at all. Four differences in the code is not decoration.

mechanism_clarity.why: A specific physical quantity - per-detector-element gain and offset deviation - with a stated reason it manifests as ring and band structure about the isocentre in a rotating-gantry geometry, a specific extractor derived from that geometry (high-pass, polar resample about isocentre, angular average), a specific validation protocol borrowed with its operating metrics, and a specific removal experiment. This is what the rubric's level 5 describes.

identifiability.why: Cross-protocol identification and the nesting test are genuine discriminators between device and protocol, and the different-patient reference protocol genuinely excludes anatomy. But device and site are nearly collinear and probably cannot be separated in LIDC, and if devices are not operated at multiple protocols in the corpus the central discrimination is unavailable. Three, not higher.

interest.why: If scanner confounding has device-level granularity, then a large body of published stratified analyses - including two candidates in this very portfolio - are under-adjusted, and the standard defence does not work. That is broadly consequential. The forensics-to-medicine transfer is also genuinely unexploited.

medical_relevance.why: Real but indirect. It changes how confounding is controlled and how multi-site generalisation is assessed; no patient is diagnosed differently tomorrow. Held to 3 honestly rather than inflated by the interest score.

clarity.why: The question names the physical quantity, the survival condition and the removal test in one sentence. Held below 5 because 'a medical imaging model' is unspecified - which model, trained on what - and that has to be fixed before Stage 2 means anything.

candidates.priority_arithmetic: Mode C weighting: 0.30*5 (mechanism) + 0.25*3 (ident) + 0.20*5 (interest) + 0.15*3 (med) + 0.10*4 (clarity) = 1.50+0.75+1.00+0.45+0.40 = 4.10. NOTE: Mode C weighting differs from Modes A and B; this number is comparable to C4's 3.95 and NOT to C1, C2 or C3.

feasibility.why: CAPPED at 3 by the keystone but assigned 2 on the merits, which is lower than the cap requires. The extractor does not exist, its physical validity on reconstructed clinical CT is unverified, the required DICOM tag is probably stripped, and Stage 2 is under-specified. Per the charter this is not a demotion - Mode C exists for candidates like this - but it should not be represented as a few weeks of work.

novelty_confidence.why: CAPPED at 3. The forensics precedent is real and a decade old, so the novelty is confined to the medical-auditing connection and to device-level granularity. I could not read the three Kharboutly papers, so I do not actually know whether they already claim device-level identification - if they do, the novelty shrinks to Stage 2 alone.

data_readiness.why: LIDC-IDRI is CC BY 3.0, fully public, no application, and small enough to download in full. This is the most readily available data in the portfolio; the uncertainty is about what is inside the headers, not about access.

evaluation_readiness.why: The PRNU literature supplies the detection-metric convention and operating points, which is more than most Mode C candidates have. But the CT-specific extractor has no accepted evaluation and Stage 2 has no established protocol.

negative_result_value.why: A decisive negative validates a control that the rest of this portfolio leans on, and can be stated as an equivalence against the forensics literature's operating points. Conditional on the corpus containing multi-protocol devices.

regret.why: Worth considering rather than obvious in hindsight. The forensics literature has been sitting there for a decade and medical imaging has not read it, but the practical consequence depends on a device-level result that may simply not hold.

candidates.recommendation: PAUSE - run Stage 0 only. It is one case download and a header dump, it costs an hour, and it determines whether either version of the study is possible. Do not commit further until Stage 2 has been specified concretely enough to be more than a forensics replication.
unverified_claims: Which DICOM tags survive TCIA de-identification for LIDC-IDRI. Device Serial Number and Station Name are ordinarily removed by the Basic Confidentiality Profile, which would fail the keystone's first form. ONE HOUR TO CHECK and it gates everything.
Whether the angularly-averaged radial noise-residual extractor works at all on reconstructed clinical CT. Entirely unverified - it is a physically motivated proposal, not a demonstrated method.

The actual content, method and claimed granularity of the three Kharboutly papers. I located the records but could not read them: the EUSIPCO PDF was image-only and no text extraction is available here. If they already demonstrate device-level identification, the novelty collapses to Stage 2.
Whether any LIDC device was operated at multiple protocol settings, without which device and protocol cannot be separated and the study is uninterpretable rather than negative.
Whether any LIDC site operated multiple same-model scanners, without which device and site cannot be separated.

Whether ring-artifact correction is applied during reconstruction on these scanners, which would suppress the very signal being sought and could explain a null for an uninteresting reason. This should be checked before a negative is reported.
Which clinical model Stage 2 would use, and whether fingerprint subtraction leaves its clinical predictions intact. Unspecified.

portfolio_level_honesty.what_i_am_least_sure_of: That C2 and C3 are two candidates rather than one. They share a corpus, a download, an author's afternoon and a conclusion structure - 'a thing that is not the patient predicts the label.' I have argued they have separable failure modes and I believe that, but a critic who merges them would not be wrong, and the portfolio would then be four candidates and short of the Mode B quota. I would rather state that now than defend it later.
portfolio_level_honesty.the_strongest_single_verified_fact_this_: The CT-CLIP preprocessing pipeline applies no body or lung masking anywhere - full volume, clipped at exactly minus one thousand Hounsfield units, resampled and cropped to 480 by 480 by 240 - read directly from the official inference script. That single fact is what turns C2 from a rhetorical question into an executable one, and it took one file fetch.
portfolio_level_honesty.the_most_useful_thing_i_killed: Question 8, the embedding-geometry candidate, which I wanted to write and which arXiv:2604.04133 appears to have already answered. Recording the kill is more useful to the next cycle than another candidate would have been.
portfolio_level_honesty.standing_gap_for_the_next_cycle: Two cycles have now failed to produce a vascular or tubular candidate despite the charter naming it as an emphasis. The blocker is the same both times: no public corpus pairing vascular or airway CT with named clinical descriptors rather than segmentation masks. This should be a dedicated dataset-scouting errand with its own output, not another line in a quota_note.
